content: The 10th Annual Safe Patient Handling and Movement Conference is scheduled to take place from March 29 to April 2, 2010. This event, partially sponsored by the American Nurses Association (ANA), will be held at the Buena Vista Palace Hotel & Spa, located within the Walt Disney World Resort in Lake Buena Vista, Florida. The primary goal of this conference is to reduce workplace injuries in healthcare settings by disseminating information on safe patient handling practices. The term Safe Patient Handling refers to programs and research aimed at minimizing work-related injuries among healthcare professionals. Nurses, aides, orderlies, and other healthcare workers who frequently lift patients are at high risk of sustaining injuries to their knees, back, shoulders, and other joints and muscles due to the physical demands of their roles. Alarmingly, the injury risk for healthcare workers surpasses that of high-risk professions such as timber cutting and construction work. This conference is designed to provide valuable insights for direct healthcare providers, administrators, risk managers, educators, managers, industrial hygienists, safety professionals, and researchers who are focused on safety issues in patient care environments. Attendees will have the opportunity to learn safe patient handling techniques through workshops and hands-on practice sessions. Additionally, they will be exposed to cutting-edge innovations from around the globe. Conference materials will include a Safe Patient Handling textbook, cognitive aids and tools, and other educational resources. Topics to be covered in the sessions include Low Back Pain Development and Patient Handling, Top Ten Research Findings for Safe Patient Handling: Reader’s Digest Version of Science over the Past Decade, Linking Patient Safety to Caregiver Safety, American Nurses Association (ANA) Initiatives for Safe Patient Handling in the USA, Practical Implementation of Patient Lift Teams, Challenges in Safe Patient Handling in Emergency Departments, Risks and Solutions for Safe Patient Handling in Operating Rooms, and many others. A complete agenda for the conference is available on the event’s website. By the conclusion of the conference, participants are expected to have acquired the ability to implement best practices for patient care, evaluate potential solutions for patient movement, and identify common ergonomic hazards in patient care. Furthermore, attendees will be equipped to develop risk reduction strategies and assess the cost and necessity of interventions in routine patient movement activities.
